maintainer_note: Policy is data here, never code. Update this file, not the verifier. Every rule carries the source it came from and the operative sentence verbatim. If a rule cannot be quoted from a primary source it does not belong in this file.

staleness_contract.rationale: The October 2025 practice took effect without a migration period. A gate silently applying superseded repository rules is worse than no gate, so the verifier refuses to certify once this file passes its horizon and requires the live policy to be re-read.

quotes.scope: arXiv's computer science (CS) category has updated its moderation practice with respect to review (or survey) articles
quotes.carve_out: These are scientific research papers and are not subject to this moderation practice change.
quotes.documentation: please include the peer reviewed journal reference and DOI metadata.
quotes.workshop_excluded: the review conducted at conference workshops generally does not meet the same standard of rigor of traditional peer review
quotes.consequence: If you do not provide this, your review article or position paper will likely be rejected.
quotes.resubmission: Do not resubmit your position paper or review article without an accepted appeal.

sources.verified_scope_note: The announcement names the computer science category. Extension to other archives was not established as of the retrieval date and must be re-checked rather than assumed.

applies_to.note: Evaluated against the primary category and every cross-list. Selecting a non-cs primary while cross-listing into cs does not remove a cs-scoped practice from the submission.

excludes.note: The announcement exempts scientific research papers on the societal impact of science and technology. The exemption is for papers of that kind, not for anything merely filed in cs.CY, so a manuscript claiming it must actually be one.

rules.content_type_basis_note: The announcement names review/survey articles and position papers. Perspective and research-programme pieces are not named and are included here as constructions of 'position paper', because they make the same move: they argue a stance about a field rather than report primary research. Treat a trigger on a construed type as a reason to re-examine the manuscript's content type, not as a quotation of policy.

requirement_detail.peer_review_doi: Acceptance at a peer-reviewed journal or conference, supplied as journal reference and DOI in the submission metadata. Workshop review does not satisfy this.

rules.consequence: Likely rejected and not announced. The author may not simply resubmit; an appeal must be accepted first, and an appeal is entertained only once peer review has completed successfully.

non_rules.statement: No rule in this file blocks a deposit for disclosing AI assistance, and none should be added. Generative AI is cited by arXiv as a cause of submission volume, not as an independent ground for rejecting a submission. Editing a disclosure to reduce its visibility is misrepresentation and is out of scope for this gate.
non_rules.verified: No arXiv policy rejecting a submission for disclosed AI assistance was located as of 2026-09-08.

evidence.claim: Machine-text detectors are not a sound basis for any gate.
evidence.source: Liang, Yuksekgonul, Mao, Wu, Zou. GPT detectors are biased against non-native English writers. Patterns 4(7), 2023.
evidence.finding: Widely-used detectors consistently misclassified non-native English writing samples as AI-generated while classifying native samples correctly; simple prompting both reduced the bias and evaded the detectors.

non_rules.statement: math, quant-ph, stat, physics and other archives carry no equivalent content-type practice in this ruleset. Absence of a rule here means the policy was not found, not that one does not exist; re-verify before relying on it for a specific archive.
